// ---- audio properties ----------------------------------------------------

/// `volume` is a linear gain and may exceed 1, up to 32 (spec §5.2, §11 AU-1).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct AudioProps {
    pub volume: f64,
    pub muted: bool,
    pub fade_in: Ticks,
    pub fade_out: Ticks,
    pub duck: Option<Duck>,
    pub mono: bool,
    /// Preserve pitch when the clip's speed is not 1.
    pub keep_pitch: bool,
    /// -1 hard left, 0 centred, +1 hard right.
    pub pan: f64,
    pub compressor: Option<Compressor>,
    /// How much background noise to remove: 0 is off, 1 the most the
    /// platform will do.
    pub noise_reduction: f64,
    /// The shape of `fade_in` and `fade_out` (format 29, spec §11 AU-114),
    /// each written only when not `linear`, so an older file's text holds.
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "FadeShape::is_linear")]
    pub fade_in_shape: FadeShape,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "FadeShape::is_linear")]
    pub fade_out_shape: FadeShape,
    /// The clip's true-peak limiter (format version 30, spec §11 AU-21),
    /// last in the tap's chain; absent is off, and is not written.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub limiter: Option<Limiter>,
    /// How much of Apple's isolated voice replaces the clip's own sound,
    /// 0 off … 1 all of it (format 31, spec §11 AU-50), written only when
    /// not 0 so an older file's text holds. The render is Swift's, offline.
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "is_zero")]
    pub isolation: f64,
            harmonics: 4,
        }
    }
}

/// Which channels of a stereo source play (spec §11 AU-34): `left` and
/// `right` copy that channel into every channel, `swapped` exchanges them.
/// A one-channel track ignores it, as it does pan.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum AudioChannels {
    #[default]
    Both,
    Left,
    Right,
    Swapped,
}

impl AudioChannels {
    pub fn is_both(&self) -> bool {
        *self == AudioChannels::Both
    }
}

/// The downward expander/gate (spec §11 AU-40, AU-43): below
/// `threshold_db` (dB relative to the clip's measured loudness, AU-41) the
/// level is pushed down by `ratio − 1` dB per dB under, never more than
/// `range_db`; `hold` keeps it open after the level falls, `attack` opens it
/// and `release` closes it. The DSP is the Swift side's.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct Gate {
    /// dB re the clip's loudness: −40…0.
    pub threshold_db: f64,
    /// 1…20.
    pub ratio: f64,
    static let shapeNames: [String] = ShapeKind.allCases.map { $0.rawValue }
    private static let audioPatchDescription: String =
        "Audio properties to merge. Keys: volume (0–"
        + String(format: "%g", AudioNormalize.maxGain) + ", 1 = unity), muted, fade_in, "
        + "fade_out (ticks), fade_in_shape and fade_out_shape (linear — the default — "
        + "s_curve, plus_3db for a fast start, minus_3db for a slow one), duck (null or "
        + "{level, attack, release, mode, pre_roll, hold}: mode extent — the default, for "
        + "the clip's whole length — or speech, only while the clip's speech plays, "
        + "widened by pre_roll before and hold after, in ticks, 0.5 s each by default; "
        + "speech saves the media's speech spans from its detected speech in the same "
        + "step, and is an error for a clip that is not a media clip with sound or whose "
        + "speech has not been detected yet), mono, keep_pitch, "
        + "pan (-1 hard left … +1 hard right), compressor (null or {threshold_db, ratio, "
        + "attack, release, makeup_db} — the two times in ticks), noise_reduction (0–1), "
        + "limiter (null or {ceiling_db, release}: a true-peak limiter last in the clip's "
        + "chain, ceiling_db in dBTP after the clip's base volume, -24 to 0, default -1, "
        + "release in ticks, 600 to 600000, default 60000; {limiter: {}} turns it on at "
        + "the defaults), "
        + "isolation (0–1: voice isolation, Apple's on-device voice model, which also "
        + "reduces room echo; 0 off, 0.8 the app's default, 1 leaves silence between words; "
        + "rendered offline, the clip plays without it until the render lands and an export "
        + "waits for it; a clip not at ×1 plays without it)" + audioEQClause
        + audioDynamicsClause + audioVoiceClause + ". duck, "
        + "compressor, limiter, eq (and each of its slots), hum, gate, leveller, de_esser and "
        + "voice are OBJECTS and they "
        + "MERGE: a key you leave out keeps what is stored, and {duck: null} clears the "
        + "whole thing."
    // Format 32's keys (spec §11 AU-31..AU-34), their own typed local so the
    // chain above stays short enough to type-check quickly. The presets' values

     3	/// The Volume section's loudness half (spec §11 AU-15): the Loudness and At
     4	/// volume readouts and the Normalize row's mode and target. The readout reads
     5	/// through the pane's `loudnessMemo` (`ClipLoudness.Memo`), so a live Volume
     6	/// or Pan drag reads no file and decodes no plan per tick; At volume is the
     7	/// held answer plus the current base volume, through `AudioLimiterModel` while
     8	/// the clip's limiter is on (AU-26) — on a clip with a stage the cache leaves
     9	/// out, the last processed R0 or "≈" the cache figure (AU-64 (g)). Mode and
    10	/// target are app-wide (`NormalizeChoice`), never an edit, so neither writes
    11	/// the document.
    12	extension AudioPane {
    13	
    14	    /// The one clip the readout is about: exactly one selected clip Normalize
    15	    /// is offered for, else nothing ("—").
    16	    private var readoutClip: UInt32? {
    17	        let clips = AudioPane.normalizable(binding)
    18	        return clips.count == 1 && binding.clips.count == 1 ? clips[0].id : nil
    19	    }
    20	
    21	    private func loudnessAnswer() -> ClipLoudness.Answer {
    22	        guard let clip = readoutClip, let document = binding.document else { return .unavailable }
    23	        return loudnessMemo.answer(for: clip, in: document)
    24	    }
    25	
    26	    /// "−41.7 LUFS · −18.5 dBTP", "measuring…" or "—"; `gain` in dB is added
    27	    /// to both (At volume). With `limiter`, the loudness is the model's at that
    28	    /// gain and the peak is held at the limiter's ceiling (AU-24, AU-26).
    29	    private func loudnessText(gain: Double, limiter: LimiterProps? = nil) -> String {
    30	        switch loudnessAnswer() {
    31	        case .pending: return "measuring…"
    32	        case .unavailable: return "—"
    33	        case .reading(let reading):
    34	            return levelText(
    35	                lufs: reading.lufs, truePeak: reading.truePeak, steps: reading.steps,
    36	                peaks: reading.stepPeaks, gain: gain, limiter: limiter)
    37	        }
    38	    }
    39	
    40	    /// One reading's figures at `gain` dB, through `limiter` when there is one.
    41	    private func levelText(
    42	        lufs measured: Double?, truePeak: Double, steps: [Double], peaks: [Double], gain: Double,
    43	        limiter: LimiterProps?
    44	    ) -> String {
    45	        guard gain.isFinite else { return "silent" }
    46	        var peak = truePeak > 0 ? 20 * log10(truePeak) + gain : -.infinity
    47	        var lufs = measured.map { $0 + gain }
    48	        if let limiter, measured != nil {
    49	            let ceiling = pow(10, limiter.ceilingDb / 20)
    50	            peak = min(peak, limiter.ceilingDb)
    51	            lufs = AudioLimiterModel.integrated(
    52	                steps: steps, peaks: peaks, gain: pow(10, gain / 20), ceiling: ceiling,
    53	                releaseSeconds: Double(limiter.release) / Double(ReelTime.perSecond))
    54	        }
    55	        let peakText = peak.isFinite ? String(format: "%.1f dBTP", peak) : "−∞ dBTP"
    56	        guard let lufs else { return "— LUFS · " + minus(peakText) }
    57	        return minus(String(format: "%.1f LUFS · ", lufs) + peakText)
    58	    }
    59	
    60	    /// At volume (spec §11 AU-64 (g)): on a clip whose chain has a stage the
    61	    /// loudness cache leaves out, the last R0 measured for its plan and chain
    62	    /// (`ProcessedLoudness.Memo`) at the current volume and limiter, else the
    63	    /// cache figure marked approximate; any other clip, the cache figure.
    64	    private func atVolumeText(_ audio: AudioProps) -> (text: String, approximate: Bool) {
    65	        let cached = loudnessText(gain: audio.decibels, limiter: audio.limiter)
    66	        guard ProcessedLoudness.needsRender(audio), let clip = readoutClip,
    67	            let document = binding.document, case .reading = loudnessAnswer()
    68	        else { return (cached, false) }
    69	        guard let processed = ProcessedLoudness.Memo.shared.reading(for: clip, in: document) else {
    70	            return ("≈ " + cached, true)
    71	        }
    72	        let text = levelText(
    73	            lufs: StepLoudness.integrated(processed.steps), truePeak: processed.peaks.max() ?? 0,
    74	            steps: processed.steps, peaks: processed.peaks, gain: audio.decibels,
    75	            limiter: audio.limiter)
    76	        return (text, false)
    77	    }
    78	
    79	    static let approximateTip =
    80	        "≈ before the clip's processing; Normalize or Enhance Voice measures through it."
    81	
    82	    private func minus(_ text: String) -> String {
    83	        text.replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−")
    84	    }
    85	
    86	    /// The Loudness row (the clip's material at volume 1, pre-fader) and the
    87	    /// At volume row (the same with the base volume's gain, through the
    88	    /// clip's limiter when it has one).
    89	    func loudnessRows() -> [NSView] {
    90	        let binding = self.binding
    91	        weak var atVolume: OptionDisplayControl?
    92	        let readout = inspectorReadout(width: 160) { [weak self] in
    93	            guard let self else { return "—" }
    94	            let answer = self.atVolumeText(binding.audioProps)
    95	            atVolume?.toolTip = answer.approximate ? AudioPane.approximateTip : nil
    96	            return answer.text
    97	        }
    98	        atVolume = readout
    99	        return [
   100	            inspectorRow(
   101	                "Loudness", [inspectorReadout(width: 160) { [weak self] in
   102	                    self?.loudnessText(gain: 0) ?? "—"
   103	                }]),
   104	            inspectorRow("At volume", [readout]),
   105	        ]
   106	    }
   107	
   108	    /// The Normalize row: Mode (Peak | Loudness) and Target (LUFS, −50…−5,
   109	    /// quick −14, −16, −23; live only in Loudness). A change re-titles
   110	    /// `button`'s tooltip and refreshes the pane.
   111	    func normalizeRow(updating button: OptionButtonControl) -> NSView {
   112	        button.toolTip = AudioPane.normalizeTip()
   113	        let modes = AudioNormalize.Mode.allCases
   114	        let popup = OptionPopupControl(
   115	            width: 96, items: ["Peak", "Loudness"],
   116	            read: { modes.firstIndex(of: NormalizeChoice.mode) ?? 0 },
   117	            write: { [weak self, weak button] index in
   118	                NormalizeChoice.mode = modes[max(0, min(index, modes.count - 1))]
   119	                button?.toolTip = AudioPane.normalizeTip()
   120	                self?.inspector?.refresh(isLive: false)
   121	            },
   122	            enabled: { true }, onEdit: {})
   123	        let range = AudioNormalize.targetLUFSRange
   124	        let target = OptionFieldControl(
   125	            width: InspectorMetrics.fieldWidth, unit: "LUFS", decimals: 1,
   126	            min: range.lowerBound, max: range.upperBound,
   127	            quick: AudioNormalize.targetLUFSQuickPicks,
   128	            read: { NormalizeChoice.targetLUFS },
   129	            write: { [weak self, weak button] value in
   130	                NormalizeChoice.targetLUFS = min(max(value, range.lowerBound), range.upperBound)
   131	                button?.toolTip = AudioPane.normalizeTip()
   132	                self?.inspector?.refresh(isLive: false)
   133	            },
   134	            enabled: { NormalizeChoice.mode == .loudness }, onEdit: {})
   135	        return inspectorRow("Normalize", [popup, target])
   136	    }
   137	
   138	    /// The button's tooltip in the chosen mode. Two of the sentences are the
   139	    /// limits, and they are here because this is where somebody meets them:
   140	    /// the tool's description says the same things (road map 2 phase 5c,
   141	    /// D-C3). The nest clause is a limit turned around: a nest alone leaves
   142	    /// the button disabled, but a nest picked BESIDE an ordinary clip leaves it
   143	    /// enabled and the nest quietly not asked about.
   144	    static func normalizeTip() -> String {
   145	        let rest =
   146	            ". It REPLACES the volume rather than adding to it, so pressing it twice "
   147	            + "changes nothing; it writes the clip's base level even while the playhead "
   148	            + "is inside an action; and it leaves Mute alone. A nest is skipped: its "
   149	            + "level lives in the clips inside it, not in the nest."
   150	        switch NormalizeChoice.mode {
   151	        case .peak:
   152	            let level = String(format: "%.0f dBFS", AudioNormalize.defaultPeakDB)
   153	            return "Set each selected clip's volume so its loudest moment reaches "
   154	                + level.replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−") + rest
   155	        case .loudness:
   156	            let target = String(format: "%.1f LUFS", NormalizeChoice.targetLUFS)
   157	            let ceiling = String(format: "%.0f dBTP", AudioNormalize.ceilingDBTP)
   158	            return ("Set each selected clip's volume so its integrated loudness reaches " + target
   159	                + ", turning the clip's limiter on at " + ceiling + " where its true peak would "
   160	                + "pass it, and stopping short where the volume would pass "
   161	                + AudioNormalize.maxGainName)
   162	                .replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−") + rest
   163	        }
   164	    }
   165	}

196	   196	    /// cannot be: the plan flattens a nest, so the clip has no segment of its
197	   197	    /// own and `read` can only refuse it. A command that can only refuse is a
198	   198	    /// command that should not be enabled (the same rule the Normalize

201	   201	    ///

215	   215	    /// Reads a document's snapshot, plan and peak caches for `clips`.
216	   216	    ///
217	   217	    /// `clips` is the caller's list — the pane passes the selected clips that
218	   218	    /// carry audio, the tool passes its `clips` argument. nil takes the
219	   219	    /// document's own selection, which is the sheet-less equivalent of
220	   220	    /// `SilenceDetector.read`'s selection override.
221	   221	    ///
222	   222	    /// nil is answered only when the core emitted a plan this build cannot
223	   223	    /// read — the same failure `CompositionBuilder` treats as fatal. A clip
224	   224	    /// that simply cannot be normalised is a `Problem`, not a nil.
225	   225	    static func read(from document: ProjectDocument, clips: [UInt32]? = nil) -> Input? {
226	   226	        // The EDITED project: a clip inside a nest is normalised against the
227	   227	        // plan of the project it is IN, which is the only one holding an
228	   228	        // audio segment for it (road map 2's phase 9).
229	   229	        guard let plan = document.editedProject.plan else { return nil }
230	   230	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
231	   231	        let loader = MediaPeaks.loader(cacheDirectory: document.cacheDirectory)
232	   232	        let segments = audioSegments(in: plan)
233	   233	
234	   234	        var readings: [Reading] = []
235	   235	        var problems: [Problem] = []
236	   236	        var seen: Set<UInt32> = []
237	   237	        for id in clips ?? document.selection.sorted() where seen.insert(id).inserted {
238	   238	            if let problem = admit(id, in: snapshot, segments: segments) {
239	   239	                problems.append(problem)
240	   240	                continue
241	   241	            }
242	   242	            guard let cited = segments[id] else { continue }  // `admit` vouched for it
243	   243	
244	   244	            // A missing peaks file means UNKNOWN, never silent: the cache is
245	   245	            // written by a fire-and-forget task at open, so a project opened a
246	   246	            // second ago or a just-relinked movie has none. Measuring against
247	   247	            // it would compute a gain from a peak of 0 — the one failure this
248	   248	            // feature must not have — so it is refused by name, and the caller
249	   249	            // is told to ask again.
250	   250	            var loudest = 0.0
251	   251	            var missing = false
252	   252	            for segment in cited {
253	   253	                guard let peaks = loader.value(for: segment.media) else {
254	   254	                    missing = true
255	   255	                    break
256	   256	                }
257	   257	                let window = MediaPeaks.peak(
258	   258	                    peaks, over: segment, from: segment.start,
259	   259	                    to: segment.start + segment.duration,
260	   260	                    reversedPivot: MediaPeaks.reversedPivot(for: segment, in: snapshot))
261	   261	                loudest = max(loudest, Double(window))
262	   262	            }
263	   263	            guard !missing else {
264	   264	                problems.append(
265	   265	                    Problem(
266	   266	                        clip: id,
267	   267	                        reason: "is still being analysed — its waveform has not been written "
268	   268	                            + "yet. Try again in a moment."))
269	   269	                continue
270	   270	            }
271	   271	            // Exactly 0 is not quiet, it is nothing: there is no gain that
272	   272	            // makes silence reach a level, and `target / 0` is an infinity
273	   273	            // that would be written as a volume.
274	   274	            guard loudest > 0 else {
275	   275	                problems.append(
276	   276	                    Problem(
277	   277	                        clip: id,
278	   278	                        reason: "is silent over the part of it that plays, so there is no level "
279	   279	                            + "to normalise."))
280	   280	                continue
281	   281	            }
282	   282	            readings.append(Reading(clip: id, media: cited[0].media, peak: loudest))
283	   283	        }
284	   284	        return Input(readings: readings, problems: problems)
285	   285	    }

290	   290	    /// the conservative reading (the clip ends up quieter than asked,

303	   303	    /// else the refusal by name — not a clip, a nest, no audio segment, no
304	   304	    /// audio props. What is read off the cache after this is each mode's own.
305	   305	    static func admit(
306	   306	        _ id: UInt32, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, segments: [UInt32: [PlanSegment]]
307	   307	    ) -> Problem? {
308	   308	        guard let clip = snapshot.clip(id) else {
309	   309	            return Problem(clip: id, reason: "is not a clip in this project.")
310	   310	        }
311	   311	        // A nest is refused HERE rather than by the segment test below,
312	   312	        // and the reason is the message. A nest clip is audible — its own
313	   313	        // volume and mute multiply every voice under it (`audio.rs`) — but
314	   314	        // the plan flattens it, so every segment it plays carries an INNER
315	   315	        // clip's id and `segments[id]` is empty for the nest itself. The
316	   316	        // generic refusal would therefore say "plays no sound in this
317	   317	        // timeline" about a clip the user can hear, which is the one thing
318	   318	        // a refusal must not do; and there is no level to measure anyway,
319	   319	        // because the peaks cache is per MEDIA and a nest holds clips that
320	   320	        // each have their own.
321	   321	        if case .nest = clip.source {
322	   322	            return Problem(
323	   323	                clip: id,
324	   324	                reason: "is a nest, and a nest has no level of its own to measure: the "
325	   325	                    + "waveform cache is per media file and the clips inside a nest "
326	   326	                    + "each have their own. Un-nest it (⇧⌘G), normalize the clips "
327	   327	                    + "inside, and nest them again — or set the nest clip's own volume "
328	   328	                    + "by hand.")
329	   329	        }
330	   330	        guard let cited = segments[id], !cited.isEmpty else {
331	   331	            return Problem(
332	   332	                clip: id,
333	   333	                reason: "plays no sound in this timeline, so there is no level to "
334	   334	                    + "measure. A still, a clip whose media has no audio track and a "
335	   335	                    + "clip with audio switched off all read this way.")
336	   336	        }

339	   339	        // otherwise reach a dialog from a button press. It cannot happen
340	   340	        // for a clip that has a segment — `add_clip` gives an audio group
341	   341	        // to exactly the clips whose media has sound — but a project is
342	   342	        // JSON somebody may have edited, and the pre-check costs a line.
343	   343	        guard clip.audio != nil else {

351	   351	    /// The ops, from a reading and a target level. Pure arithmetic: no
352	   352	    /// document, no disk, no AppKit.
353	   353	    ///
354	   354	    /// `peakDB` is the caller's, validated by the caller — the pane passes the
355	   355	    /// constant and the tool refuses anything outside `peakDBRange` by name. A
356	   356	    /// non-finite one would put a NaN in every volume, so it falls back to the
357	   357	    /// default here and the fallback is REPORTED as `Plan.peakDB`, the way
358	   358	    /// `detect_silence` names back the settings it actually ran with.
359	   359	    static func plan(_ input: Input, peakDB: Double = defaultPeakDB) -> Plan {
360	   360	        let level = peakDB.isFinite ? peakDB : defaultPeakDB
361	   361	        // Double `pow`, not `AudioDSP.gain(fromDecibels:)`: that one is the
362	   362	        // render thread's single-precision fast path, written so a per-sample
363	   363	        // conversion costs one `expf`. This is a model value, computed once
364	   364	        // and stored in the project.
365	   365	        let target = pow(10, level / 20)
366	   366	
367	   367	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
368	   368	        var normalized: [Result] = []
369	   369	        for reading in input.readings {
370	   370	            let wanted = target / reading.peak
371	   371	            let volume = min(maxGain, max(0, wanted))
372	   372	            ops.append(.setAudio(clips: [reading.clip], patch: AudioPatch(volume: volume)))
373	   373	            normalized.append(
374	   374	                Result(
375	   375	                    clip: reading.clip, media: reading.media,
376	   376	                    measuredDB: decibels(reading.peak), volume: volume,
377	   377	                    resultDB: decibels(reading.peak * volume), clamped: wanted > maxGain))
378	   378	        }
379	   379	        return Plan(peakDB: level, ops: ops, normalized: normalized, skipped: input.problems)
380	   380	    }

383	   383	    /// `AudioProps.decibels`, which is about a gain rather than about a peak —
384	   384	    /// one line, two subjects, and no shared home worth making for it.
385	   385	    private static func decibels(_ magnitude: Double) -> Double {
386	   386	        magnitude <= 0 ? -.infinity : 20 * log10(magnitude)
387	   387	    }

552	   164	    /// true peak fits the ceiling at `v0` gets `volume: v0` alone (AP1's
553	   165	    /// result). Any other gets one `set_audio {volume, limiter}`: its own
554	   166	    /// limiter kept, the ceiling lowered to −1 dBTP when above it, or the
555	   167	    /// default; the volume is `AudioLimiterModel`'s gain for the target under
556	   168	    /// that limiter. `limited_by` is `max_gain` when the volume ceiling stops
557	   169	    /// it short. It may turn a clip down. A non-finite target falls back to
558	   170	    /// the default and is reported as `targetLUFS`. A clip in `solved` was
559	   171	    /// measured through its chain (AU-64) and takes its solve's volume and
560	   172	    /// limiter instead (`solvedRow`).
561	   173	    static func plan(
562	   174	        _ input: LoudnessInput, targetLUFS: Double = defaultTargetLUFS,
563	   175	        solved: [UInt32: Solved] = [:]
564	   176	    ) -> LoudnessPlan {
565	   177	        let target = targetLUFS.isFinite ? targetLUFS : defaultTargetLUFS
566	   178	        let ceiling = pow(10, ceilingDBTP / 20)
567	   179	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
568	   180	        var normalized: [LoudnessResult] = []
569	   181	        for reading in input.readings {
570	   182	            if let solve = solved[reading.clip] {
571	   183	                let (op, row) = solvedRow(reading, solve)
572	   184	                ops.append(op)
573	   185	                normalized.append(row)
574	   186	                continue
575	   187	            }
576	   188	            let wanted = pow(10, (target - reading.lufs) / 20)
577	   189	            let first = max(0, min(wanted, maxGain))
578	   190	            let row: LoudnessResult
579	   191	            if reading.limiter == nil, reading.truePeak * first <= ceiling {
580	   192	                ops.append(.setAudio(clips: [reading.clip], patch: AudioPatch(volume: first)))
581	   193	                row = LoudnessResult(
582	   194	                    clip: reading.clip, media: reading.media, measuredLUFS: reading.lufs,
583	   195	                    truePeakDBTP: 20 * log10(reading.truePeak), volume: first,
584	   196	                    resultLUFS: reading.lufs + 20 * log10(first),
585	   197	                    resultTruePeakDBTP: 20 * log10(reading.truePeak * first),
586	   198	                    limit: wanted <= maxGain ? nil : .maxGain, limiter: nil)
587	   199	            } else {
588	   200	                var limiter = reading.limiter ?? LimiterProps()

     2	
     3	/// Enhance Voice (road map "audio" AP6, spec §11 AU-60…AU-62, AU-64):
     4	/// measurements in, ordinary settings out. Clip ▸ Enhance Voice, the Volume
     5	/// section's Enhance Voice button (both through `AudioMeasureDoor`) and the
     6	/// agent's `enhance_voice` call `read`, `choose` and `jobs`, run the jobs
     7	/// through a `LoudnessMeasureRun`, and `plan` over its outcome —
     8	/// `AudioNormalize`'s seam and posture: no door does arithmetic, so the
     9	/// three cannot mean different things, and the rules can be checked without
    10	/// a window (`audio_ap6_probe.py`).
    11	///
    12	/// **What it measures** (AU-61) is pre-chain: the clip's `ClipLoudness`
    13	/// reading — L, the true peak, each 10 ms played step's energy, true peak,
    14	/// source midpoint and high band — split into speech and pause steps by the
    15	/// media's speech spans (`media.speech`, else the VAD cache's
    16	/// `DuckSpeech.spans`). Nothing it reads depends on a key it writes, so a
    17	/// second press writes the same values and the core answers an identity.
    18	///
    19	/// **What it writes** (AU-60, AU-62, AU-67): one `set_audio` per clip, its
    20	/// BASE props, owning exactly nine keys — `eq` (Rumble Cut on the clip's own
    21	/// EQ), `isolation`, `noise_reduction`, `gate`, `leveller`
    22	/// (`AudioEnhance+Leveller.swift`), `de_esser`, `compressor`, `limiter` and
    23	/// `volume`; every other key is left as it is. Volume and
    24	/// limiter are solved on the clip rendered through the chosen settings
    25	/// (AU-64), as Loudness Normalize solves a processed clip, so Normalize after
    26	/// Enhance changes nothing either.
    27	enum AudioEnhance {
    28	    static let actionName = "Enhance Voice"
    29	    /// AU-62: a floor less than this under L cleans and gates; at or under it,
    30	    /// the pauses are already quiet.
    31	    static let noisyGapDB = -45.0
    32	    /// The gate opens this far above the pauses' median true peak.
    33	    static let gateAbovePausePeakDB = 10.0
    34	    /// The gate's threshold, dB re L, is held here.
    35	    static let gateThresholdRange = -40.0 ... -6.0
    36	    /// A speech step whose high band reads at least L + this is sibilant.
    37	    static let sibilanceGapDB = -10.0
    38	    /// The de-esser goes on at this share of sibilant speech steps.
    39	    static let sibilanceShare = 0.05
    40	    /// 1 s of speech, in 10 ms steps: under it there is no voice to measure.
    41	    static let minimumSpeechSteps = 100
    42	    /// 0.5 s of pause: under it there is no floor.
    43	    static let minimumPauseSteps = 50
    44	    /// Noise reduction's amount where isolation cannot serve the clip.
    45	    static let noiseReductionAmount = 0.5
    46	
    47	    /// One clip's measurements (AU-61), before any rule.
    48	    struct Measurement: Equatable {
    49	        /// The `ClipLoudness` reading's integrated LUFS and linear true peak.
    50	        let lufs: Double
    51	        let truePeak: Double
    52	        let speechSteps: Int
    53	        let pauseSteps: Int
    54	        /// The median pause-step loudness, LUFS (−∞ allowed); nil under
    55	        /// `minimumPauseSteps`.
    56	        let floorLUFS: Double?
    57	        /// The median pause-step true peak, dBFS (−∞ allowed); nil with the floor.
    58	        let pausePeakMedianDB: Double?
    59	        /// The share of speech steps whose high band reads ≥ L + `sibilanceGapDB`.
    60	        let sibilantShare: Double
    61	        /// The median speech-step true peak, dBFS.
    62	        let peakMedianDB: Double
    63	        /// Every segment of the clip `IsolationCache.isolatable`.
    64	        let isolatable: Bool
    65	        /// The speech's short-term loudness range, LU (AU-67); nil under 3 s.
    66	        let speechRangeLU: Double?
    67	
    68	        /// floor − L, dB; nil without a floor.
    69	        var floorGapDB: Double? { floorLUFS.map { $0 - lufs } }
    70	    }
    71	
    72	    /// What `read` took for one clip.
    73	    struct Reading: Equatable {
    74	        let clip: UInt32
    75	        let media: UInt32
    76	        let measurement: Measurement
    77	        let loudness: ClipLoudness.Reading

    79	        /// limiter whose ceiling is kept.

    85	        let problems: [AudioNormalize.Problem]
    86	
    87	        var isEmpty: Bool { readings.isEmpty }
    88	    }
    89	
    90	    /// One clip's settings before its volume (AU-62): `patch` writes neither
    91	    /// volume nor limiter; `limiter` is the one the solve uses and the edit
    92	    /// writes.

    94	        let clip: UInt32
    95	        let media: UInt32
    96	        let measurement: Measurement
    97	        let patch: AudioPatch
    98	        let limiter: LimiterProps

   100	    }

   102	    /// What one clip's enhance will do.
   103	    struct Row: Equatable {
   104	        let clip: UInt32
   105	        let media: UInt32
   106	        let measurement: Measurement
   107	        let patch: AudioPatch
   108	        /// One sentence per rule: the measurement, the threshold, what it set.
   109	        let reasons: [String]
   110	        /// Normalize's row for the volume and limiter (AU-62's last rule).
   111	        let loudness: AudioNormalize.LoudnessResult
   112	        /// R0's loudness through the chosen settings, and the renders the
   113	        /// solve took (AU-64).
   114	        var processedLUFS: Double? { loudness.processedLUFS }
   115	        var renders: Int { loudness.renders }
   116	    }
   117	
   118	    struct Plan {
   119	        /// The target after `plan`'s finiteness guard — what actually ran.
   120	        let targetLUFS: Double
   121	        let ops: [ReelOp]
   122	        let enhanced: [Row]
   123	        let skipped: [AudioNormalize.Problem]
   124	
   125	        var isEmpty: Bool { ops.isEmpty }
   126	    }
   127	
   128	    // MARK: - Reading
   129	
   130	    /// Reads the document's edited project, plan and caches for `clips` (nil:
   131	    /// the selection). nil only for a plan this build cannot read; a clip that
   132	    /// cannot be enhanced is a problem, by name (AU-60).
   133	    static func read(from document: ProjectDocument, clips: [UInt32]? = nil) -> Input? {
   134	        guard let plan = document.editedProject.plan else { return nil }
   135	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
   136	        let loader = ClipLoudness.loader(cacheDirectory: document.cacheDirectory)
   137	        let segments = AudioNormalize.audioSegments(in: plan)
   138	        var readings: [Reading] = []
   139	        var problems: [AudioNormalize.Problem] = []
   140	        var seen: Set<UInt32> = []
   141	        func skip(_ id: UInt32, _ reason: String) {
   142	            problems.append(AudioNormalize.Problem(clip: id, reason: reason))
   143	        }
   144	        for id in clips ?? document.selection.sorted() where seen.insert(id).inserted {
   145	            let answer = ClipLoudness.answer(
   146	                for: id, snapshot: snapshot, segments: segments, loader: loader)
   147	            guard case .reading(let loudness) = answer else {
   148	                if answer == .pending {
   149	                    skip(id, "is still being analysed — its loudness has not been measured "
   150	                        + "yet. Try again in a moment.")
   151	                } else {
   152	                    problems.append(
   153	                        AudioNormalize.admit(id, in: snapshot, segments: segments)
   154	                            ?? AudioNormalize.Problem(
   155	                                clip: id, reason: "plays no sound in this timeline."))
   156	                }
   157	                continue
   158	            }
   159	            guard loudness.playedTicks >= ClipLoudness.minimumPlayedTicks else {
   160	                skip(id, "plays for under 0.4 s, too short for an integrated loudness (one "
   161	                    + "400 ms gating block).")
   162	                continue
   163	            }
   164	            guard loudness.lufs != nil, loudness.truePeak > 0 else {
   165	                skip(id, "is under −70 LUFS over the part of it that plays, so there is no "
   166	                    + "voice to enhance.")
   167	                continue
   168	            }
   169	            let own = (segments[id] ?? []).filter { $0.media == segments[id]?.first?.media }
   170	            let mediaID = own.first?.media ?? 0
   171	            guard let media = snapshot.media(mediaID),
   172	                let spans = media.speech ?? speechSpans(media, cache: document.cacheDirectory)
   173	            else {
   174	                skip(id, "is still being analysed — its speech has not been detected yet. Try "
   175	                    + "again in a moment.")
   176	                continue
   177	            }
   178	            let mask = speechMask(sources: loudness.stepSources, spans: spans)
   179	            guard
   180	                let measurement = measure(
   181	                    loudness, speech: mask, isolatable: own.allSatisfy(IsolationCache.isolatable))
   182	            else {
   183	                skip(id, "has under 1 s of speech over the part of it that plays, too little "
   184	                    + "to measure a voice from.")
   185	                continue
   186	            }
   187	            readings.append(
   188	                Reading(
   189	                    clip: id, media: mediaID, measurement: measurement, loudness: loudness,
   190	                    current: snapshot.clip(id)?.audio ?? AudioProps()))
   191	        }
   192	        return Input(readings: readings, problems: problems)
   193	    }
   194	
   195	    /// The media's speech spans off its VAD cache, nil while it is not written.
   196	    static func speechSpans(_ media: MediaSnapshot, cache: URL?) -> [[Ticks]]? {
   197	        guard let cache, let p = MediaImporter.loadSpeech(for: media.id, in: cache) else {

   364	    static func plan(
   365	        _ input: Input, choices: [Choice], outcome: LoudnessMeasureRun.Outcome,
   366	        targetLUFS: Double

   368	        let target = targetLUFS.isFinite ? targetLUFS : AudioNormalize.defaultTargetLUFS

     3	/// Enhance Voice's leveller rule (spec §11 AU-67): the speech's short-term
     4	/// loudness range, and whether it turns the leveller on.
     5	///
     6	/// **The range** is measured pre-chain, like everything Enhance reads
     7	/// (AU-61): the clip's 10 ms steps where the speech mask is true,
     8	/// concatenated, in 3 s windows (`shortTermSteps`) at a 0.1 s hop
     9	/// (`shortTermHopSteps`); each window's loudness is `StepLoudness.loudness`
    10	/// of its mean energy. EBU Tech 3342's gating applies — absolute −70 LUFS,
    11	/// then −20 LU under the energy mean of what passed — and the range is the
    12	/// 95th percentile less the 10th, each linearly interpolated (numpy's
    13	/// default). Under one window of speech there is none.
    14	///
    15	/// **The rule.** Over `levellerRangeLU` Enhance writes the leveller at its
    16	/// defaults; at or under it, null; with no range the key is left out of the
    17	/// edit. Each case has its sentence. A second press measures the same range,
    18	/// so it writes the same value (AU-61's idempotence).
    19	extension AudioEnhance {
    20	    /// Over this range the leveller goes on.
    21	    static let levellerRangeLU = 6.0
    22	    /// A short-term window, 3 s of 10 ms steps.
    23	    static let shortTermSteps = 300
    24	    /// The windows' hop, 0.1 s.
    25	    static let shortTermHopSteps = 10
    26	    /// EBU Tech 3342's two gates, LUFS and LU.
    27	    private static let rangeAbsoluteGate = -70.0
    28	    private static let rangeRelativeGate = -20.0
    29	
    30	    /// The speech's short-term loudness range in LU, from each step's energy
    31	    /// and the speech mask; nil under `shortTermSteps` speech steps or when
    32	    /// every window is gated out.
    33	    static func speechRange(steps: [Double], speech: [Bool]) -> Double? {
    34	        let count = min(steps.count, speech.count)
    35	        var energies: [Double] = []
    36	        energies.reserveCapacity(count)
    37	        for k in 0..<count where speech[k] { energies.append(steps[k]) }
    38	        guard energies.count >= shortTermSteps else { return nil }
    39	        var windows: [Double] = []
    40	        var sum = energies[0..<shortTermSteps].reduce(0, +)
    41	        var start = 0
    42	        while true {
    43	            windows.append(sum / Double(shortTermSteps))
    44	            let next = start + shortTermHopSteps
    45	            guard next + shortTermSteps <= energies.count else { break }
    46	            // Summed afresh at each hop: no running drift over a long clip.
    47	            sum = energies[next..<(next + shortTermSteps)].reduce(0, +)
    48	            start = next
    49	        }
    50	        let passed = windows.filter { StepLoudness.loudness($0) >= rangeAbsoluteGate }
    51	        guard !passed.isEmpty else { return nil }
    52	        let relative = StepLoudness.loudness(passed.reduce(0, +) / Double(passed.count))
    53	            + rangeRelativeGate
    54	        let levels = passed.map(StepLoudness.loudness).filter { $0 >= relative }.sorted()
    55	        guard !levels.isEmpty else { return nil }
    56	        return percentile(levels, 0.95) - percentile(levels, 0.10)
    57	    }

    59	    /// The `p` quantile of sorted `values`, linearly interpolated between the
    60	    /// two nearest ranks (numpy's default).
    61	    private static func percentile(_ values: [Double], _ p: Double) -> Double {
    62	        let position = p * Double(values.count - 1)
    63	        let low = Int(position.rounded(.down))
    64	        let high = min(low + 1, values.count - 1)
    65	        return values[low] + (values[high] - values[low]) * (position - Double(low))
    66	    }
    67	
    68	    /// AU-67's rule over one measurement: the leveller to write (nil: the key
    69	    /// is left out; `.some(nil)`: off) and its sentence.
    70	    static func levellerRule(_ m: Measurement) -> (leveller: LevellerProps??, reason: String) {
    71	        let line = String(format: "%g LU", levellerRangeLU)
    72	        guard let range = m.speechRangeLU else {

    78	            return (.some(LevellerProps()), "Leveller: \(measured), above \(line), so the "
    79	                + "leveller is on at its defaults.")
    80	        }
    81	        return (.some(nil), "Leveller: \(measured), at or under \(line), so the leveller is off.")
    82	    }
    83	}

7:There is only one kind of track. Any track can hold a clip with sound, whether it is a video file, an audio-only file (a voice-over, music, a recorder's take) or a clip you split off with Detach Audio. A clip with sound shows its waveform in the timeline.

55:A nest clip has the same Sound sub-tab, but not every control reaches the clips inside it:
227:Voice Isolation keeps the voice and removes what is around it: background noise, music, and the echo of the room. It uses Apple's on-device voice model, so nothing leaves your Mac.
235:At 80 % the pauses between words drop by about 14 dB and keep a little of the room, so the voice doesn't sit in dead silence. At 100 % the pauses are silent. Isolation also reduces room echo, so there is no separate de-reverb control.
254:| Space | **Echo** repeats it every quarter of a second; **Room**, **Hall**, **Plate** and **Cathedral** put it in a space, from a small room to a long cathedral tail. |
267:The effect comes right after Voice Isolation: an isolated clip's effect is made from its isolated voice, so it waits for that first. Everything after it in the list (the channel choice, the EQ, noise reduction and the rest) works on the effected sound.
269:The effect plays only on a clip at normal speed, as Voice Isolation does. A reverb or an echo stops at the end of the clip; it doesn't ring on into the next one.
271:*Agents:* `set_audio` with `voice`: `{kind, amount, pitch}`, where `kind` is `pitch`, `high`, `deep`, `robot`, `bass`, `treble`, `bright`, `telephone`, `radio`, `lofi`, `distorted`, `echo`, `room`, `hall`, `plate` or `cathedral`; `amount` 0–1 (1 if left out); `pitch` −12 to 12, for `pitch`, `high` and `deep`. A new `kind` keeps a stored `pitch` unless `pitch: null` is sent with it, and `voice: null` turns the effect off. The render's status isn't in `get_project`; an export waits for it.
279:Use Left Only or Right Only for a microphone recorded onto one channel of a stereo file: the voice then plays from both speakers at its own level, and the Volume section's Loudness read-out counts it that way. The choice comes right after voice isolation, before the EQ and the mono fold. A mono file has only one channel, so the choice has no effect on it.
425:## Mix: pan, mono, Detach Audio and Attach Audio
432:| Detach Audio | Moves the clip's audio onto its own clip (see below). | — | — |
433:| Attach Audio | Merges a detached sound back into its picture (see below). | — | — |
444:### Detach Audio
446:**Clip ▸ Detach Audio** (⌥⌘D), or the **Detach Audio** button in the Mix section, splits each selected clip's sound onto a clip of its own on the track below. If the clip is already on the bottom track, Frame Job adds a new track underneath for it.
452:Detach Audio is refused, with the reason given, for a clip that isn't a media clip, a clip whose file has no audio track, and a clip whose audio is already switched off. It's also refused when the track below already has a clip where the new audio clip would go. A new track is added only when the clip is on the bottom track.
456:*Agents:* `detach_audio` (`clip`). `set_enabled` (`clip`, `video`, `audio`) turns either half of a clip back on or off.
466:- **Delete** on the picture deletes its sound too. Deleting the sound alone keeps the picture, silent. Detach Audio and then deleting the sound is how you remove a clip's sound.
467:- **Speed** and **Reverse** are refused on a linked clip: "clip … is linked to clip …: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction". Attach Audio first, change the speed, then detach again.
479:When the shot before was detached too, its sound sits on the same track as this one's, so a lead would overlap it and become a cross dissolve. **Drag the sound to a track of its own first**, then trim it: on its own track, the lead overlaps nothing.
485:**Clip ▸ Attach Audio** (⇧⌥⌘D), or the **Attach Audio** button in the Mix section, merges each detached sound in the selection back into its picture. Either clip can be selected. The picture's audio comes back on with the sound clip's audio settings, and the sound clip is removed. Its track stays.
487:Attach Audio is refused for a clip that isn't linked to a detached sound, and for a pair that no longer covers the same time, such as a J-cut or an L-cut: "clip …'s picture and clip …'s sound do not cover the same time; trim them to match before Attach Audio". Trim the two to the same start and end, then attach.
598:The meter includes everything that shapes what you hear: each clip's volume, fades, ducking, mute and solo, and the compressor and other effects. At normal speed it shows the mix itself, so two tracks playing the same sound read as one louder sound, and a sound and its inverse read as silence. At other speeds it adds up each track's level, which can read a little higher than the mix. When playback stops, the bars fall back to the floor. If two projects are open, the meter follows the one that is playing. On a very narrow window there isn't room for the meter, so it is hidden.
713:- A voice effect also plays only at normal speed. A clip has one effect at a time. A reverb or echo tail ends with the clip, and a clip split from a take starts its effect fresh at the cut. The waveform, the Loudness read-out and Remove Silences hear the clip without its effect; Normalize in Loudness mode measures through it. On a stereo file a reverb or an echo mixes the two channels, so the channel choice picks from the effected pair.
727:- Loudness mode's result for a limited clip with no other processing is a model of the limiter, read from the loudness analysis; the export lands within a few tenths of a LU of it (−15.9 LUFS for the −16 example above). A clip measured through its processing is checked by rendering, so its result is the render's.
730:- Match Audio matches the average tone of the speech, not the room, its reverb, its noise or its dynamics, and only with the EQ's five shelves and bands. It matches clips to a clip, not to a track or a mix, and the sheet doesn't remember its last choice.

89:Every clip with sound, except a nest clip, draws a thin white line over its waveform: the level you hear from that clip over time. It is the clip's volume and its volume actions, with the fades, crossfades, ducking and the track's volume folded in. The top of the clip's audio part is +30 dB (3200 %) and the bottom is −60 dB or quieter. A clip you can't hear, because it's muted, its track is muted, another track is soloed or its sound is switched off, has its line along the bottom. The line starts below the action lane and is drawn only where the audio part is at least 12 pt tall, so at the Small track height it may not show. A small square in the action colour marks each action end that sets the volume.
419:Each clip's limiter holds that clip alone. Every export also runs a **master limiter** over the whole mix, the same kind of limiter at −1 dBTP (or the export's own ceiling), so two limited clips crossfading, a nest turned up or an action raising a clip's volume still can't take the file past it. The preview has no master limiter. See [Exporting](export.md#loudness).
497:## Crossfading audio across a transition
499:When two clips on one track overlap with a transition, the transition can also crossfade their sound. Turn on **Crossfade Audio** in the clip's Transition section. The crossfade keeps the combined loudness steady across the overlap. See [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md).
552:A track can have its own **compressor** and **limiter**, below Pan in the same panel (the fifth header switch, **Mix…** in the track's right-click menu, or **Track ▸ Mix…**). They act on the track's whole sound: every clip on it, after each clip's own processing, its volume, fades, crossfades and ducking, and after the track's volume and pan. The compressor runs first, then the limiter, whose ceiling is the highest true peak the track hands the mix.
571:- **Approximate in the preview.** The preview plays a track's sound in more than one piece where its clips overlap (a crossfade, or a nest's tracks), and it runs the compressor and limiter on each piece separately, so the pieces can add up past a track limiter's ceiling while editing. Measured on two clips at −1 dBFS crossfading under a limiter at −6 dBTP, the preview's true peak was 5.2 dB over the ceiling; the export held it. The Loudness Meter says "approximate" while any track has a compressor or limiter.
709:- A track's compressor and limiter are approximate in the preview wherever its clips overlap (a crossfade, a nest's tracks); see [Track compressor and limiter](#track-compressor-and-limiter). A nest's own tracks have none, and scrubbing doesn't hear them.

89:Every clip with sound, except a nest clip, draws a thin white line over its waveform: the level you hear from that clip over time. It is the clip's volume and its volume actions, with the fades, crossfades, ducking and the track's volume folded in. The top of the clip's audio part is +30 dB (3200 %) and the bottom is −60 dB or quieter. A clip you can't hear, because it's muted, its track is muted, another track is soloed or its sound is switched off, has its line along the bottom. The line starts below the action lane and is drawn only where the audio part is at least 12 pt tall, so at the Small track height it may not show. A small square in the action colour marks each action end that sets the volume.
419:Each clip's limiter holds that clip alone. Every export also runs a **master limiter** over the whole mix, the same kind of limiter at −1 dBTP (or the export's own ceiling), so two limited clips crossfading, a nest turned up or an action raising a clip's volume still can't take the file past it. The preview has no master limiter. See [Exporting](export.md#loudness).
497:## Crossfading audio across a transition
499:When two clips on one track overlap with a transition, the transition can also crossfade their sound. Turn on **Crossfade Audio** in the clip's Transition section. The crossfade keeps the combined loudness steady across the overlap. See [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md).
552:A track can have its own **compressor** and **limiter**, below Pan in the same panel (the fifth header switch, **Mix…** in the track's right-click menu, or **Track ▸ Mix…**). They act on the track's whole sound: every clip on it, after each clip's own processing, its volume, fades, crossfades and ducking, and after the track's volume and pan. The compressor runs first, then the limiter, whose ceiling is the highest true peak the track hands the mix.
571:- **Approximate in the preview.** The preview plays a track's sound in more than one piece where its clips overlap (a crossfade, or a nest's tracks), and it runs the compressor and limiter on each piece separately, so the pieces can add up past a track limiter's ceiling while editing. Measured on two clips at −1 dBFS crossfading under a limiter at −6 dBTP, the preview's true peak was 5.2 dB over the ceiling; the export held it. The Loudness Meter says "approximate" while any track has a compressor or limiter.
709:- A track's compressor and limiter are approximate in the preview wherever its clips overlap (a crossfade, a nest's tracks); see [Track compressor and limiter](#track-compressor-and-limiter). A nest's own tracks have none, and scrubbing doesn't hear them.
